rationale: Internally consistent in sign, but it is essentially a mechanical rank-sum of three separately published anomalies (Sloan accruals, earnings smoothness, cash-based profitability) with no genuine interaction, and the nested SUMRANK silently gives accruals double the weight of the other legs.

The interaction logic is coherent and the sign matches the expression, but dividing by a five-year earnings volatility that can be arbitrarily close to zero makes the signal explosive and outlier-driven (and amplifies negative accruals as much as positive ones), so a rank-space or vol-quintile-conditioned version would test the same idea far more reliably.

A legitimate, sign-consistent state-contingent test of whether the accrual premium requires an improving cash-profitability trajectory, though the multiplicative indicator dumps all deteriorating-cash firms at exactly zero, creating a large tie mass in the middle of the sort that will blur the long-short spread and should be replaced by a signed or demeaned conditioning term.

The two legs are near-mechanically related and partly contradictory — the indicator frequency rewards persistently negative accruals while the absolute-accrual term penalizes exactly those large negative gaps — and the 6-level moving average carries little cross-sectional dispersion, so the composite reduces to a noisy |accruals| sort rather than the claimed "habitually clean" state.

This is a direct rediscovery: leg one is textbook Sloan working-capital accruals and leg two is Novy-Marx gross profitability, additively combined, which is a standard published quality composite rather than a cross-theme interaction (the hypothesis describes a conditional effect that the rank-sum does not actually compute).

Economically coherent and sign-consistent, but note that accruals are by construction ib/at − oancf/at, so the second leg's trend is the earnings trend minus the cash trend, meaning the signal double-loads cash-flow trend and loads *negatively* on the earnings trend — a bet against earnings momentum that should be diagnosed explicitly rather than assumed benign.
